science_vegetable: Enzymatic luciferin-luciferase oxidation gated by voltage-sensitive ion channels flashing in prime-number sequences and optical polarization modulation.
text:
The ultraviolet aurora pulsed overhead, washing the ironwood grove in sickly magenta light. Kaio lunged over a fallen silicon-based vine, his boots skidding across the slick ferro-moss. The twin-sun magnetic cycle was narrowing. If the grid stripped entirely before he reached the ridge, the telemetry in his hand would evaporate. The canister rattled against his ribs. Inside, the fungal cluster fired off another sharp sequence. Blue-blue-green. Pause. Red.

His breath burned in his lungs. He slapped his hand against a basalt outcropping to arrest his momentum. His fingers slipped on a viscous secretion covering the stone. The secretion smelled of copper and ozone. A shadow detached itself from the canopy overhead. A hex-pedal carapace, shifting its oil-slick armor to match the auroral glare, dropped directly into his path. The creature’s mandibles clicked, a sound like glass fracturing under pressure. He was cut off from the main ascent path.

A cold, diamond-hard focus snapped down over Kaio’s chaotic racing mind. His jaw tightened. He did not draw the sonic emitter at his belt. He looked at the canister in his left hand. The specimen inside communicated through enzymatic luciferin-luciferase oxidation, gated by voltage-sensitive ion channels. It did not glow randomly; it flashed in prime numbers. The predator’s multiple eyes contracted and expanded, tracking the ambient ultraviolet radiation. Kaio gripped the canister's base ring.

He twisted the optical polarization filter to maximum throughput. The seal cracked. A blinding, strobing pulse of white light erupted into the grove, modulating furiously through the prime syntax. The hex-pedal creature recoiled, its front legs thrashing as the intense optical overload overwhelmed its ocular cavities. Kaio ducked under the flailing limbs, scrambling up the loose scree of the incline. His boots found purchase on the upper trail.

He sprinted toward the bunker airlock. He hit the manual release, throwing his shoulder against the heavy steel door. He stumbled inside, sealing the lock behind him. He stood in the antechamber, the cold tactical focus shattering into breathless, scattered energy. His pulse hammered wildly. He jogged down the corridor toward the kitchens, the glowing canister still gripped tightly in his hands. The sharp scent of roasted tubers and chitinous fungi drifted through the ventilation grating. He stepped over the threshold. Ryn stood over a massive iron cauldron. Before she could speak, Kaio grabbed the secondary water filter housing from the wall rack. He dumped a handful of the glowing fungal spores into the active carbon mesh. 'This will optimize the viscosity!' he shouted, immediately unscrewing the primary valve. Algae-sludge erupted across the counter. Ryn grabbed a clean sock from the supply crate with a look of pure murder.
